THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSIO 07.08.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 2 MACA 157/2019  2025:KER:59925  JUDGMENT (Dated this the 7th day of August 2025)
The petitioner has filed this appeal seeking an enhancement of the compensation awarded for the injuries sustained in a motor accident.
The original claim was filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

2. On 3.10.2010 at about 6.30 am., the appellant was travelling as a pillion rider on a motor cycle bearing reg.No.KL- 49/9881 from Mathur side to Pulinelly side and when he reached near Pulinelly Anganavadi, another motor cycle bearing reg.No.KL-10-L-2250 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner, dashed on the motor cycle and due to the accident, the appellant suffered grievous injuries and fractures.

Immediately, he was taken to the Malabar hospital,
Palakkad and thereafter, was referred to the Medical college hospital, Thrissur.
He was treated there as inpatient till 25.10.2010.

3. The 1st respondent, who is the RC owner of the offending vehicle, was set ex-parte and the 2nd respondent filed written statement denying his negligence and disputing the quantum of compensation claimed in the petition.
It is contended that the accident happened due to the negligence of the appellant himself.

The vehicle was insured with the 3rd respondent, who 2025:KER:59925 filed a separate written statement admitting the policy of the motor cycle with registration No.KL-10-L-2250, but it was contended that the 2nd respondent was not having a valid driving license at the time of accident.
4. The evidence consisted of Ext.Nos.A1 to A19 series.
There was no oral evidence from the side of the appellant.
From the side of 3rd respondent, RW1 was examined and Exts.B1 series and B2 were marked and Ext.X1 was marked as 3rd party Exhibit.

The Tribunal, considering the facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of documentary and oral evidence, awarded a compensation of Rs.2,17,500/- with interest at 9% pa from the date of petition till realisation.

The 3rd respondent was authorized to recover the compensation amount paid, from the 1st respondent Bhaskaran (Died) vs Abdul Jaleel on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121426527/
2 by the Tribunal.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded, this appeal is filed by the claimant.

5. The counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was aged 38 years at the time of accident,
earning Rs.6,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has taken only Rs.4,000/- per month as notional income of the appellant.

The Counsel for the appellant submits that even going by the decision reported in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited [(2011) 13 SCC 236], the 2025:KER:59925 notional income of a coolie who met with an accident in the year 2010 is to be taken as 7,500/-, in the absence of any evidence.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited [(2011) 13 SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The counsel for the 1st respondent opposed to the same and submitted that since the claim is only for Rs.6,000/- the Tribunal has rightly taken the notional income as Rs.4,000/- and the benefit of the judgment relied on Ramachandrappa (supra) cannot be granted to the appellant.
Therefore, no interference is warranted.

6. In Rajesh v. Rajbir Singh [(2013) 9 SCC 54], the apex court held that even though the claim is for a lesser amount, the Tribunal has to fix a just compensation and therefore, the monthly income fixed by the decision in Ramachandrappa (supra) has to be taken in the absence of any documentary evidence.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the notional income of the appellant can be fixed as Rs.7,500/- per month.

Hence, taking the said income, physical disability at 7% and the multiplier as 15 (since the appellant falls between the age group of 36-40), the compensation for permanent disability is calculated as 7500 x 12 x 15 x 7/100 = 94,500/-.

7. The Tribunal has found that since the appellant was inpatient for 97 days for different periods and since the appellant has suffered type II open fracture Tibia and Fibula, he would have 2025:KER:59925 taken rest for 10 months and therefore, under the head of loss of earning for 10 months is to be calculated.
Thus. Taking Rs.7,500/- as the monthly income, the loss of earning would come to 7,500 x 10 = 75,000/-.
8. A perusal of the order of the Tribunal shows that just and reasonable compensation is awarded under all other heads.

9. Accordingly, the following enhancements are made to the award passed by the Tribunal:
Sl. Head of Claim Amt. Awarded by Amt. Enhanced No. Tribunal (Rs.) in appeal (Rs.)
1 Compensation for permanent 50,400 94,500 disability 2. Loss of earning 40,000 75,000 90,400 1,69,500 Amount enhanced- 1,69,500- 90400=79,100/-
In the result, this appeal is allowed and the appellant is entitled for an enhanced amount of Rs.79,100/- (Rupees seventy nine thousand and one hundred only).
The Insurance Company shall pay interest for the enhanced amount at the rate of 9% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation.
All other findings 2025:KER:59925 entered by the Tribunal stand confirmed.
If any amounts have already been paid, the same shall be granted set off.
The claimants shall produce the details of the Bhaskaran (Died) vs Abdul Jaleel on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/121426527/

3 Bank account before the Insurance Company/Tribunal within one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment and amount shall be transferred to the Bank account directly through NEFT/RTGS mode, within a period of one month thereafter.
If the Bank account is not furnished within the time stipulated, it is made clear that no interest shall run on the enhanced amount after the period stipulated by this Court.

It is also made clear that the appellant would not be entitled for interest for the period of delay of 130 days in filing the Appeal, as per order of this Court dated 15.11.2024, on the enhanced compensation.
It is also made clear that the direction to the 3rd respondent to recover the compensation paid, is also kept in tact.

Sd/-
BASANT BALAJI, JUDGE dl/
